question: Can information about entity #11+ become unreachable BECAUSE it was omitted from the parent summary?
separate_finding: ~33% of bare entity-name queries do not surface their evidence at top-10 in either mode, INDEPENDENT of summary membership (control 38.8% unreachable vs omitted 30.8%). Belongs to P16 RETRIEVAL-QUALIFICATION, not to the entity cap.
degradations_observed: none. All lanes live for every query: document_summary_routing, section_summary_routing, global_child, reranker, lexical (HYBRID), plus region_demotion and global_child_rescue where applicable. Reranker confirmed genuinely active (real g3 scores, pre_g3_order != post_g3_order). The result is therefore measured with the full lane set, not a degraded one.
mechanism: parent_summaries.entities is read on NO retrieval path (zero references in pass1.py, hybrid.py, api/fast.py, api/retrieve.py).
Section routing embeds retrieval_summaries.summary_text, which is prose extracted from the source. The entity list is a separate payload field and never enters the embedded text.

Therefore membership in the top-10 entity list cannot influence whether a section is routed to. The empirical contrast confirms it: omission changes unreachability by -8.0 points, i.e. omitted entities fare slightly BETTER than in-summary controls.
Recovery of omitted evidence arrives via MULTI_REPRESENTATION (36), GLOBAL_CHILD_RESCUE (8) and SECTION_LED (4) - never via a summary-entity lookup, because no such lookup exists.
